name: Taiwan Contemporary Culture Lab (C-LAB)
funding: State: run since 2018 by the Ministry of Culture's Taiwan Living Arts Foundation; budget figure not found.
watch: State-funded lab; roster not checked. Funder is the Ministry of Culture via its foundation. Only criticism found: a gentrification complaint.
records_note: Its operator, Taiwan Living Arts Foundation, posts annual reports 2018 to 2025, financial statements, a donations and subsidies list and its trustees.

name: Bangkok Art Biennale
funding: BAB Foundation, chaired by ThaiBev CEO Thapana Sirivadhanabhakdi; ThaiBev is main partner, with Siam Piwat and Central Group (2018). Venice 2026 show adds Bangkok city, TAT, BEM, Ch. Karnchang, Generali.
watch: Alcohol money (ThaiBev, Fraser and Neave, SABECO) is no flag. Bangkok city, a partner, censored a July 2025 BACC show, not the biennale.
records_note: No reports or accounts found; sponsors show as undated logos without names, and the BAB Foundation page lists its board members.

name: Thailand Biennale
funding: 2025-26 edition: Ministry of Culture's Office of Contemporary Art and Culture with Phuket province; commissions co-funded by unnamed foundations.
watch: State-run; commissions co-funded by unnamed foundations. The archived Partners page (Nov 2025) has placeholder logos only. The live site is behind a Vercel bot check. No controversy found for the Phuket edition.
records_note: Could not check: the biennale site returned 403 and 429 blocks, so nothing was confirmed beyond its government organisers.

name: Alice Yard
location: Port of Spain, Trinidad and Tobago
funding: Mellon Foundation USD 150,000 over 36 months (awarded February 2024). Nordic Culture Fund and OCA support residencies; co-rd Ltd and Basso Leonard Architects are listed supporters.
watch: Artist-run space in Belmont, Port of Spain, 20 years old in 2026. Trinbagonians for Palestine supported a 2025 screening.
records_note: The blog's sidebar names two supporters, co-rd Ltd and Basso Leonard Architects, with no date; no reports, accounts or board are published.

name: B7L9 Art Centre
funding: Run by the Kamel Lazaar Foundation, set up in 2005 by Swicorp founder Kamel Lazaar, a Riyadh-based investment banker; B7L9 opened in 2019 as its first permanent venue. The foundation's undated partners page names the German Federal Foreign Office, the EU delegation, Goethe-Institut, Pro Helvetia, Institut Français, Tunisair and the Tunisian Education Ministry.
watch: Swicorp is a Riyadh-based investment bank, not a state body. Lazaar once sat on the board of Creative Energy Resources, a power-sector holding. No controversy found for the foundation or Lazaar.
records_note: No reports or accounts found; the parent Kamel Lazaar Foundation names 18 partners and funders on an undated page and its founders and staff, but no board.

name: Pera Museum
watch: Whether the foundation holds Koç assets is unknown.
records_note: The Suna and Inan Kirac Foundation posts a 2025 activity report and names its six-member board; no donor list or audited accounts found.

name: RAK Art Foundation
funding: Al Qasimi Foundation, primarily funded by the Ruler of Ras Al Khaimah.
watch: Gulf ruler's body; labour critique not checked.

name: The Common Guild
funding: £379k income (FY2025). Creative Scotland plus grants from Ampersand, Henry Moore, Elephant Trust, Pro Helvetia, British Council Scotland, Goethe-Institut, Culture Ireland, Hope Scott Trust and individuals.
watch: Its thanks list names Outset; a November 2024 open letter asked Tate to divest from it. No current Outset credit found.
records_note: No annual reports, only a diversity report; OSCR holds accounts 2021 to 2025; the support page names funders undated; the board is listed.

name: Delfina Foundation
funding: £1.4M income (FY2025): partnership income £751k, grants and donations £546k. Partners include Mondriaan Fund, Samdani Art Foundation, Charles Wallace India Trust, Brooks Foundation, Inlaks Shivdasani; galleries and patron networks.
watch: Saudi Arabia's Visual Arts Commission is a named 2026 residency partner (Intermix); amounts are not itemised.
why_flagged: £1.4M income (FY2025): partnership income £751k, grants and donations £546k. Partners include Mondriaan Fund, Samdani Art Foundation, Charles Wallace India Trust, Brooks Foundation, Inlaks Shivdasani; galleries and patron networks.
records_note: Names current partners and supporters with no date and four trustees; no annual reports posted, accounts filed with the register for 2024 and 2025.

name: Mosaic Rooms
funding: Fully funded by the A.M. Qattan Foundation to date. Al-Qattan Charitable Trust paid for the 2026 refit and is the family foundation's largest donor. Independent charity since February 2026.
watch: Qattan wealth comes from Kuwaiti construction. Director Pip Day's 2024 dismissal from a Concordia gallery concerned a film screening, not funding.
records_note: No annual reports found; accounts are on the Charity Commission register, the footer names Al-Qattan Charitable Trust undated, and eight trustees are listed.

name: Akron Art Museum
funding: $5.4M expenses (2023); private donors, foundations and members.
watch: FirstEnergy Foundation is a current key supporter. FirstEnergy's own generation is 99% coal, and it paid a $230M fine over Ohio's HB6 bribery case. No protest found.
why_flagged: FirstEnergy Foundation is a current key supporter. FirstEnergy's own generation is 99% coal, and it paid a $230M fine over Ohio's HB6 bribery case. No protest found.
records_note: Its Form 990 is public for 2001 to 2025 and it lists its board and names key supporters undated, but posts no annual reports.

name: Bronx Museum of the Arts
funding: $4.3M expenses (FY2025). Public: NYC Cultural Affairs, NYSCA, NEA, IMLS. Corporate and foundation: Con Edison, Bank of America, Bloomberg Philanthropies, Deutsche Bank Americas Foundation, Ford, Warhol and Luce foundations.
watch: No adverse funder finding; roster not checked. Bloomberg Philanthropies and Deutsche Bank Americas Foundation are on the roster. 2016: two executives and four trustees resigned.
records_note: Names supporters with no date and lists its trustees; no annual report or accounts on the site, Form 990s for 2001 to 2025 on ProPublica.
